about: Rows of the master catalogue whose circuits are too long to store as columns. Each row has every field of a row of master_catalog.json except columns, plus construction, the rule that builds the columns (master_catalog/constructions.py), and columns_sha256, the SHA-256 of those columns as compact JSON in the order the rule fixes. rotation_powers is one digit per column, the power of T it runs at (1, 3, 5 or 7), or null. The header of master_catalog.json applies to these rows too: regimes, discovery, references and the rest.

families.two-group: Singh, Gidney and Jones (arXiv:2606.28518): outputs 0..k-1, checks k..N-1; one T rotation on A | B for every set A of outputs and every non-empty set B of checks with (|A| = 0 or |A| = 1 mod s_O) and |A| + |B| = 1 mod s_total; columns sorted ascending, then the list sorted lexicographically
families.san-jose-grs: San José's construction (arXiv:2609.08203) from a generalised Reed-Solomon code over F = GF(2^m), m = field_degree, elements as polynomial-basis bitmasks reduced by field_modulus. Points a = 0..L-1 (L = outer_length); r_a = 1/prod_{b != a}(a + b); v_a = r_a^(2^m/4). Generator rows (v_a a^e)_a, e = 0..D (D = outer_degree, 0^0 = 1). Eliminate on the coordinates of punctures in the given order (pivot = first row at or below the current rank that is non-zero there; swap it up, scale to 1, clear the column in every other row); if echelon is "reduced", continue on the other coordinates in increasing order, skipping any without a pivot, until every row has one. Rows 0..P-1 are g_i, the rest are h_r. Inner map phi(y)_j = parity(embedding_columns[j] & y). Wire i*|U| + t (outputs, k = P*|U|) is phi(u_t g_i), u_t = compatible_elements[t]; wire k + r*m + j (checks) is phi((1 << j) h_r); rows are restricted to the coordinates not in punctures, in increasing order, and retained coordinate p, inner bit j is column p*s + j (s = len(embedding_columns)). Column c = the wires whose row has bit c set; then every column sorted ascending and the list sorted lexicographically. k and N repeat the wire counts. Distance at least D + 2 - P.
families.san-jose-curve: San José's construction (arXiv:2609.08203) with the outer code from a curve over F = GF(2^m), m = field_degree, elements as polynomial-basis bitmasks reduced by field_modulus. K = curve_subspace (t elements, an F_2-subspace), e = curve_exponent, A = pole_order, g = (t-1)(e-1)/2. Coordinates: every (x, y) in F x F with prod_{kappa in K}(y + kappa) = x^e, ordered by x then y (there must be 2^m * t of them). Generator rows: x^i y^j evaluated at the coordinates, for j = 0..t-1 (outer) and i = 0, 1, ... (inner) with i*t + j*e <= A, 0^0 = 1. Eliminate on the coordinates of punctures in the given order (pivot = first row at or below the current rank that is non-zero there; swap it up, scale to 1, clear the column in every other row); if echelon is "reduced", continue on the other coordinates in increasing order, skipping any without a pivot, until every row has one. Rows 0..P-1 are g_i, the rest are h_r. Inner map phi(y)_j = parity(embedding_columns[j] & y). Wire i*|U| + t (outputs, k = P*|U|) is phi(u_t g_i), u_t = compatible_elements[t]; wire k + r*m + j (checks) is phi((1 << j) h_r); rows are restricted to the coordinates not in punctures, in increasing order, and retained coordinate p, inner bit j is column p*s + j (s = len(embedding_columns)). Column c = the wires whose row has bit c set; then every column sorted ascending and the list sorted lexicographically. k and N repeat the wire counts. Distance at least A - 2g + 2 - P.
families.punctured-rm: Haah and Hastings (arXiv:1709.02832): points of F_2^m are the integers 0..2^m-1, bit i being x_i; parent rows are the monomials of degree <= r evaluated at all points, ordered by degree then by itertools.combinations(range(m), d), so N = sum_{d<=r} C(m,d); punctures strictly increasing; for j = 0..t-1 with p = punctures[j], swap the first row with index >= j that is 1 at p into position j and add it to every other row that is 1 at p; rows 0..t-1 are outputs (k = t), rows t..N-1 checks; one column per surviving point listing the rows that are 1 there; columns sorted ascending, then the list sorted lexicographically
families.punctured-weighted-rm: weighted Reed-Muller parent (Wills, arXiv:2608.24000, Def. 2.15): the squarefree monomials x^a (a an m-bit mask) with sum of weights[i] over bits i of a <= cutoff, in increasing a, monomial a being 1 at point x iff x & a == a; for each puncture p in list order the first not-yet-chosen row (current order) that is 1 at p becomes the next output and is added to every other row that is 1 at p; outputs are the chosen rows in puncture order, checks the unchosen rows in parent order; one column per surviving point listing the wires that are 1 there; columns sorted ascending, then the list sorted lexicographically
families.ccz-frame: CCZ frame on RM(q-1, 3q): every point x of F_2^m (m = 3q, bit i = x_i) is a column; outputs are the monomials x_S for the q-sets S of triples, triple by triple (output 3i+j = triples[i][j]); checks are all monomials of degree <= q-1, by degree then by itertools.combinations(range(m), d); column x touches output i iff x contains S_i and check j iff x contains its variable set; the gate is CCZ on outputs (3i, 3i+1, 3i+2) and d = 2^q when each triple partitions {0..m-1} and no other three of the sets do; columns sorted ascending, then the list sorted lexicographically
families.four-block: four-block parent: S = F_2^L minus the 4-flats [o,d1,d2,d3,d4] in removed_flats, points numbered 0..M-1 in increasing order; F = the vectors on S orthogonal to 1, x_i and x_i x_j, with the basis e_j + (pivots of the rows that are 1 at j) for each non-pivot j in increasing order, after reducing those functions to echelon form with each pivot at its row's highest coordinate; coordinate b*M+i is point i in block b; parent rows (f,f,f,f) for each basis f, then (0,a,0,a), then (0,0,a,a) for a = 1, x_0..x_{L-1}; for each puncture (a coordinate) in list order the first not-yet-chosen row that is 1 there becomes the next output and is added to every other row that is 1 there; checks are the unchosen rows in parent order; one column per surviving coordinate; columns sorted ascending, then the list sorted lexicographically
families.explicit: the columns themselves: columns_zlib_b64 is the compact JSON of the list of columns (each a sorted list of wires), compressed with zlib and written in base64; they are used in the order stored
